about.title: Redondo Beach Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Redondo Beach sits where Pacific Coast Highway, Artesia Boulevard, Aviation Boulevard and Inglewood Avenue funnel South Bay traffic through a city of roughly 68,000 residents. In 2025, public records logged 235 injury collisions here, with 302 people hurt and no traffic deaths. Those crashes cluster late on Friday afternoons, between about 5 and 7 p.m., when beach traffic and commuters share the same lanes. If one of those collisions involved you, the practical questions come fast: who pays for the emergency room visit, what happens to lost wages, and whether the other driver's insurer is really on your side. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Redondo Beach residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Los Angeles County car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Before you sign anything or give a recorded statement, it helps to have someone in your corner who understands California's comparative fault rules and the two-year filing deadline.

whyChoose.title: Why Redondo Beach Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for a crash on Inglewood Avenue or Aviation Boulevard, you may still recover damages reduced by your share. An attorney can push back when an adjuster tries to inflate that share.

items.title: Deadlines that shift depending on who hit you
items.desc: Most California car accident claims must be filed within two years, but a claim involving a city bus, public works truck or other government vehicle can carry a window as short as six months. Getting connected early keeps those dates from slipping.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, and LawProactive itself is free. You can get your case reviewed without adding another bill to the ones already piling up.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Pacific Coast Highway in Redondo Beach. What should I do in the first few days?
items.answer: Get checked by a doctor even if you feel mostly fine, since neck and back symptoms often show up later. Photograph your vehicle, keep the police report number, and write down the names of anyone who saw the crash. Hold onto receipts and any messages from the other driver's insurer. Then reach out so we can connect you with an attorney before evidence fades or gets discarded.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Do I have to give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and doing so before speaking with an attorney can hurt your claim. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that make a simple answer sound like an admission of fault. Politely decline, provide only basic contact and policy details, and let an attorney handle further communication.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering after a California car accident?
items.answer: California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering and loss of enjoyment of life in an ordinary car accident case. What you can actually recover depends on the specific facts, the available insurance, and how well the evidence is preserved. An attorney can explain how those factors apply to your situation without promising any particular result.
